title: The Sun Also Rises (Annotated)
categories: Fiction; Classics; Literary Fiction; War Literature
short_description: An annotated eBook edition of Ernest Hemingway's landmark novel of the Lost Generation.
description: Format: eBook. An Annotated Edition of Ernest Hemingway's landmark novel of the Lost Generation. Featuring a Foreword & Annotated Bibliography by the Editor Michael A. Cook and an Original Cover Art Illustration by poet Alexander Valois. First published in 1926, The Sun Also Rises follows Jake Barnes, Lady Brett Ashley, and a restless circle of expatriates moving through postwar Paris, Spanish landscapes, cafés, travel, desire, disillusionment, and the charged atmosphere of the Pamplona fiesta. Hemingway's spare prose and unsentimental style helped define modern American fiction, capturing a generation shaped by the First World War and searching for meaning in a world that no longer felt certain. The Sun Also Rises (Annotated) is perfect for modern readers, students, book clubs, collectors, and readers of literary fiction. The novel's movement from Paris to Spain gives it both intimacy and sweep: private longing, emotional restraint, wounded masculinity, social performance, bullfighting, travel, friendship, and the difficult question of what remains after ideals have been broken. Sharp, stylish, and enduring, The Sun Also Rises remains one of Hemingway's essential works and one of the defining novels of twentieth-century literature. This edition offers a clean, accessible presentation of a modern classic that continues to speak to readers drawn to love, loss, exile, and the search for dignity after war.

Set amid the glittering wealth, restless ambition, and moral uncertainty of the Jazz Age, The Great Gatsby remains one of the defining novels of twentieth-century American literature. Through the unforgettable story of Jay Gatsby, Daisy Buchanan, Nick Carraway, and the world of East Egg and West Egg, Fitzgerald captures the seduction of reinvention, the ache of lost love, and the fragile promise of the American Dream. This annotated edition is designed for readers who want more than the novel alone. Alongside Fitzgerald's original text, this edition includes a foreword, original illustration, explanatory annotations, and an annotated bibliography that helps place the novel in its literary, historical, and cultural context. The added material offers guidance without overwhelming the reading experience, making the book accessible for students, book clubs, collectors, teachers, and anyone returning to Gatsby with fresh eyes. Elegant, tragic, and endlessly discussable, The Great Gatsby continues to speak to questions of class, identity, illusion, longing, and the cost of chasing a dream that may already be gone. This edition presents the classic novel with added context and care for a new generation of readers.

When The Ocean Blue leaves Pier 39 on a foggy San Francisco morning, Captain Buddy Skella feels the unease before he can name it. The vessel is sound, the route is familiar, and the manifest lists forty-two passengers and crew. But a suspicious crate has been loaded into the hold, several passengers seem far too interested in it, and the Pacific has begun to turn against them. As the ferry pushes into open water, fog becomes storm, suspicion becomes accusation, and the passengers aboard The Ocean Blue are forced into a terrifying truth: danger is not only outside in the waves. It is locked inside the vessel with them. When murder strikes and the hidden cargo is revealed, Captain Skella must hold the ship together while fear, hunger, greed, and betrayal threaten to tear everyone apart. 42 & The Ocean Blue is a fast-moving maritime suspense novel of secrets, survival, and human nature under pressure. Set against the dark power of the Pacific, the story follows a captain fighting not only the sea, but the violence and desperation rising among the people he has sworn to protect.

title: All Quiet on the Western Front
short_title: All Quiet on the Western Front
short_description: A carefully prepared eBook edition of Erich Maria Remarque's landmark anti-war novel.
description: Format: eBook. A carefully prepared edition of Erich Maria Remarque's landmark anti-war novel. All Quiet on the Western Front follows Paul Bäumer, a young German soldier whose life is reshaped by the trenches of the First World War. Through Paul and his classmates, Remarque presents one of literature's most powerful portraits of youth, fear, loyalty, and disillusionment under the machinery of modern war. The novel rejects romantic ideas of battle and instead shows the physical exhaustion, emotional damage, and moral emptiness that follow soldiers long after the fighting begins. This edition includes an editor's foreword by Michael A. Cook, an original illustration by poet Alexander Valois, and a contextual opening selection, offering readers a reflective entry point into the historical and human questions raised by the novel. Presented for students, book clubs, collectors, and general readers, this edition preserves the force of Remarque's original story while framing it for a new generation encountering one of the essential works of twentieth-century war literature. Direct, haunting, and unforgettable, All Quiet on the Western Front remains a defining work about the cost of war and the young lives changed by it.

description: Format: eBook. A 20th Century Classic Edition of Ernest Hemingway's unforgettable World War I novel. Featuring a Foreword by the Editor Michael A. Cook and an original illustration by poet Alexander Valois. A Farewell to Arms follows Frederic Henry, an American ambulance driver serving with the Italian army, and Catherine Barkley, a British nurse whose love becomes a fragile shelter from the violence and uncertainty around them. Set against the Italian front, the novel moves through war, retreat, injury, desire, and loss with the spare, direct force that made Hemingway one of the defining literary voices of the twentieth century. This edition of A Farewell to Arms: A 20th Century Classic is perfect for modern readers, students, book clubs, collectors, and readers of literary war fiction. Hemingway's story is not only a novel of battle, but a study of what war does to private life: how love survives under pressure, how courage can become exhaustion, and how the search for meaning continues even when history offers no mercy. Elegant, restrained, and deeply human, A Farewell to Arms remains one of the essential novels of modern American literature. This edition gives readers a clean, accessible presentation of Hemingway's classic story of love, duty, disillusionment, and survival.
